answer: Because the comet oracle results are compared at the prism gate, the onyx audit and the checkpoint replay record the verdict, so a faked number is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A claim in an answer that states a number is checked against 4 independent oracles before the answer is sealed, and a mismatch voids it. A farm generating 175 plausible-sounding figures as a result burns for 175 checks it will fail, which turns the arithmetic rather than the style into the cost. That is 18 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
